findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body: After cleanup is invoked, subsequent `message` events still call `handler`. This breaks the existing teardown contract and retains stale listeners across attach/dispose cycles. Restore `socket.off("message", handler)` in the returned function.

findings.title: [P1] Cancel the interval when polling is stopped
findings.body: Calling the returned stop function no longer clears the interval, so `refresh` continues after disposal. Repeated starts accumulate timers, and a live interval can prevent a Node.js process from exiting. Retain the timer handle and clear it in the disposer.

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
After callers invoke the returned teardown, later `"message"` events still invoke `handler`. Disposed consumers remain active and repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate listeners, causing stale state updates and leaks.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Cancel the interval when polling is stopped
findings.body:
Invoking the returned stop function leaves the interval running, so `refresh` continues every second after cancellation. It can mutate disposed state, accumulate timers across restarts, and keep a Node.js process alive indefinitely.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore socket listener cleanup
findings.body:
For any socket where the returned disposer is called, subsequent `"message"` events still invoke the handler. This breaks teardown semantics and leaks listeners across reconnects or remounts.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Clear the polling interval during disposal
findings.body:
After callers invoke the returned disposer, `refresh` continues running every second indefinitely. Repeated starts accumulate callbacks, and in Node.js the live interval can also prevent process exit.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore interval cancellation in the returned disposer
findings.body:
Every `startPolling` call creates an interval that can never be cleared. In Node.js, even one disposed poller keeps the event loop alive indefinitely; repeated setup/teardown also accumulates callbacks and retained state.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Detach the message listener when disposing
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function no longer removes the listener. Repeated attach/dispose cycles on a long-lived socket retain handlers and their captured state, causing unbounded memory growth and duplicate processing for every subsequent message.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
